provenance.basis: A second adult adds about 40% to everyday costs (shared housing and bills, but more food, clothes and travel), and a couple rents a place about 20% larger. Round game numbers, not from data. A partner's own pay is a choice (stays home, part-time, full-time) taken as a share of your pay; their tax is worked out separately and only their pay after tax is counted.

Yearly cost of a child in an urban middle-class family, in today's rupees for a metro: 3 lakh for the birth and first year (delivery 1 to 5 lakh plus baby costs; sources put the first year at 3 to 8 lakh), 1 lakh a year to age 2, 1.5 lakh a year for playschool and early years (an insurer's guide: 5 to 6.5 lakh for the first three years, playschool 60,000 to 1.5 lakh a year in a metro), 2 lakh a year for school and 4 lakh for college, adding to about 50 lakh by age 21 before fees outrun prices. In a tier-2 city everything is scaled to 65%. Published totals for the whole upbringing range from 50 lakh to over a crore (one blog: about 1.17 crore at 2022 prices for a middle to upper-middle family), so this is at the low end: it assumes a family that economises. A child is independent after 21. Playschool, school and college fees rise 3 points a year faster than general prices (about 7.5% a year in all): blog estimates of education inflation run from 8 to 12% and one insurer assumed 6%, so this is cautious. All from financial-services blogs and press summaries, not official data.

Illustrative family model: marriage at a chosen age, one wedding bill, a household that costs more, an optional partner's pay, and up to two children arriving at fixed gaps. Wedding sizes are in stages.json (modest 5 lakh, typical 15 lakh, lavish 40 lakh in today's rupees; WedMeGood's 2025-26 survey put the average wedding at about 39.5 lakh, skewed by large and destination weddings, and a budget calculator gave 5 to 25 lakh for a middle-class family).
